title: Would you see a 20 minute play?  Triumph is playing at the Public The...
transcript: This play is only 20 minutes long, which means I spent longer on the subway to see it than I did actually watching the play itself. So why would anyone wanna see a play so short? Well for starters, all of the tickets were free. It features Tony winner Annaleigh Ashford and her real life husband Joe Tapper, and features a pretty killer creative team including award winning playwright Caryl Churchill and award winning director Saheem Ali. But unfortunately I'm not really sure that this one worked for me. And I do think a large part of that is the fact that it is only 20 minutes. because despite being so short, it moves at a pretty break neck pace with each scene or moment, not really having a lot of time to breathe before it just has to move on to the next one. The show itself is about fascist governments and the way that they maintain power through fear and violence. And it's hardly subtle in its messaging, down to the title of the play being very similar to the name of a current political figure. And again, with more time I think they could have added in some of that subtlety and really explored some of these themes beyond just surface level observations. Which is a shame because this play should be a slam dunk. Like we just had the current administration announce that they are going to be doing a live streamed public execution and here You have a play comparing our current administration to the many fascist governments in history that have used very similar tactics. But when the play doesn't really go any deeper than that, it ends up just feeling like a missed opportunity. And don't get me wrong, I am a big fan of brevity in theatre. I love a 90 minute, no intermission. And I am a big proponent that your play should not be any longer than it needs to be. The problem is, I didn't leave this play feeling like 20 minutes was enough time for them to tell the story that they wanted to tell. And it is a rare time that I left the theatre thinking that should have been longer.
classificationReason: Creator attended this 20-minute Caryl Churchill play (free tickets) featuring Annaleigh Ashford and directly critiques its pacing and thematic depth.
